Block prose
<aside> General Usage

Semantic role: aside. Compiles to Layer 1 <aside>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <aside>
<aside | A side note about the elephant.> <aside type=warning .important | Be careful here.> <aside type=callout | This is a multi-line callout. It can contain multiple paragraphs and other content like <strong | emphasis> and inline references. > Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
type kwarg note sidebar callout warning tip info caution Optional classification of the aside’s role. Affects rendering (callouts get visual emphasis; sidebars get layout treatment). Maps to JATS via boxed-text content-type at export.
title kwarg Optional title rendered at the top of the aside (the frameable title-top convention, #31). Lifts to a child tag at the normalize-to-canonical gate; the child form is equivalent.
caption kwarg Optional caption rendered at the foot of the aside (frameable caption-bottom convention, #31), with the “Box N.” label folded in when numbered. Lifts to a <caption> child tag at the gate.
+numbered boolean default false Whether this aside is numbered. Off by default (boxed prose is usually a one-off callout). When +numbered, the aside counts in its OWN “Box N” series (the box counter / ref-prefix box), not the figure counter.
+border boolean default true Frameable surface (#31). On by default for boxed prose — the visual box is the point of a callout / sidebar. Use -border to suppress the outline.
<blockquote> General Usage

Semantic role: blockquote. Compiles to Layer 1 <blockquote>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <blockquote>
  • Markdown: > …
  • Alias: <quote> → <blockquote>
<quote | A short quotation.>

The <quote> shorthand expands to <blockquote> at Layer 1.

<quote cite=https://example.com/source | A longer quotation that may contain multiple paragraphs. The second paragraph of the quotation. > <quote type=epigraph | All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way. > <blockquote | Same as <quote> but using the explicit Layer 1 name.>

Render pending — the example source has an unescaped <…> tag-mention the parser consumes into an empty nested element (issue #277).

Authors can also write <blockquote> directly. Both forms produce the same Layer 1 output.

 Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
cite kwarg URL of the source being quoted. Maps to HTML’s standard cite attribute on
. For inline citation references (citing a bibliography entry), use a element inside the blockquote instead.
type kwarg verse dialogue epigraph pullquote other Optional classification of the quotation’s role. Affects styling and may affect JATS export.
<dd> General Usage

Semantic role: dd. Compiles to Layer 1 <dd>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <dd>
<dd | An academic publishing system built on HTML+CSS+JS.>

A definition-list description. Appears as a child of <dl>, following the term it defines.

<dd | A multi-paragraph definition. The second paragraph of the definition. >

Multi-paragraph descriptions are valid — the pipe content’s paragraph structure is preserved.

<details> General Usage

Semantic role: details. Compiles to Layer 1 <details>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <details>
<details> <summary | More background> Additional context for the curious reader. The summary is the visible heading; this body shows when the disclosure is opened. </details>

The canonical shape: a <summary> for the visible heading, followed by the disclosure body. The body is recursively parsed as prose / block content.

<details +open> <summary | Always-expanded section> This disclosure is expanded by default. </details>

The +open boolean kwarg expands the disclosure by default. Maps to HTML’s standard open attribute.

 Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
open kwarg true false HTML’s open attribute on
. When present, the disclosure is expanded by default. Either +open or open=true form works; absence (or -open / open=false) renders collapsed.
<dl> General Usage

Semantic role: dl. Compiles to Layer 1 <dl>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <dl>
<dl> <dt | enscribe> <dd | An academic publishing system built on HTML+CSS+JS.> <dt | Layer 1> <dd | The canonical semantic HTML vocabulary.> <dt | Layer 2> <dd | The shorthand authoring syntax that compiles to Layer 1.> </dl>

Long-form <dl> with short-form <dt>/<dd> children. The natural authoring pattern.

<dl .compact> <dt | term-1> <dd | First definition of term-1.> <dd | Second definition of term-1.> </dl>

One term with multiple definitions — a valid HTML pattern.

<dt> General Usage

Semantic role: dt. Compiles to Layer 1 <dt>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <dt>
<dt | enscribe>

A definition-list term. Appears as a child of <dl>.

<dt | <code | strict-mode>>

Inline markup in a term. The recursive-content pass parses the pipe content normally.

<glossary> General Usage

Semantic role: glossary. Compiles to Layer 1 <glossary>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <glossary>
<glossary #project-terms> <glossary-entry> <dt | enscribe> <dd | An academic publishing system built on HTML+CSS+JS.> </glossary-entry> <glossary-entry> <dt | Layer 1> <dd | The canonical semantic HTML vocabulary.> </glossary-entry> </glossary>

Render pending — indented long-form closing tag not recognised → tag-error (issue #276).

A glossary with two entries. Each <glossary-entry> uses <dt>/<dd> for its term and definition (the same shapes <dl> uses), wrapped in the entry’s own envelope for cross-reference / styling.

<glossary-entry> General Usage

Semantic role: glossary-entry. Compiles to Layer 1 <glossary-entry>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <glossary-entry>
<glossary-entry #term:enscribe> <dt | enscribe> <dd | An academic publishing system built on HTML+CSS+JS.> </glossary-entry>

A single glossary entry. The id uses the “term:” colon-prefix convention so cross-references like <ref @term:enscribe> can resolve into the entry.

<hr> General Usage

Semantic role: hr. Compiles to Layer 1 <hr>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <hr>
  • Markdown: ---
<hr>

Render pending — bare <hr> / <hr type=…> parsed as a long-form opener (no self-close) → tag-error (issue #275).

<hr type=scene-break>

Render pending — bare <hr> / <hr type=…> parsed as a long-form opener (no self-close) → tag-error (issue #275).

<p | First paragraph.> <hr type=ornamental> <p | Second paragraph after a thematic break.>

Render pending — bare <hr> / <hr type=…> parsed as a long-form opener (no self-close) → tag-error (issue #275).

 Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
type kwarg scene-break section-break ornamental decorative other Optional classification of the thematic break’s role. Affects rendering (scene breaks render as blank space; ornamental breaks render with decorative characters or images).
<note> General Usage

Semantic role: note. Compiles to Layer 1 <note>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <note>
Some text<note | A substantive note about the text.>. A claim<note placement=foot | A footnote.>. A definition<note placement=side | Inline-adjacent note.>. Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
placement kwarg end foot side Determines where the note content is collected. “end” collects at article-back; “foot” collects at article-back (distinguished from “end” by CSS class on the note-list); “side” renders the content inline-adjacent to the marker. Document-wide default is “end”.
position kwarg end foot side Legacy alias for “placement” (same values, same data-note-placement output). Retained for backwards compatibility; “placement” is preferred for new documents.
type kwarg substantive technical editorial translator other Optional classification. Most notes are substantive (authorial commentary).
<note-list> General Usage

Semantic role: note-list. Compiles to Layer 1 <note-list>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <note-list>

No standalone example — see the registers above and the related constructs in this chapter.

 Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
type kwarg end-notes chapter-notes footnotes-collected other
<p> General Usage

Semantic role: p. Compiles to Layer 1 <p>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <p>
<p | A simple paragraph.> A paragraph written without explicit tags.

In most cases, paragraphs do not need to be written with explicit tags. Plain markdown handles paragraph separation: blank lines delineate paragraphs. The explicit <p> form is used when attributes (id, classes, type) are needed.

<p type=lead | The opening paragraph of an article.> Arguments
attribute kind values / default notes
type kwarg normal lead intro abstract summary other Optional classification of the paragraph’s role. Mostly used for styling (lead paragraphs render larger; abstract paragraphs styled distinctly).
<summary> General Usage

Semantic role: summary. Compiles to Layer 1 <summary>.

Registers:

  • Canonical: <summary>
<summary | More background>

The visible heading of a <details> disclosure. Appears as a child of <details>.

<summary | Click to reveal the <em | hidden> details>

Inline markup in a summary. The recursive-content pass parses the pipe content normally.
